findings.title: Guard the missing destination before checking its integration
findings.body: When Google Meet is selected and destinationCalendar is null or empty, destructuring produces an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar. Reading its integration throws before the intended Cal Video fallback can run. The previous optional access supported this case; bookings with a missing or disconnected destination calendar now fail instead of falling back.

findings.title: Pass each calendar adapter its matching destination
findings.body: Every host's credential is invoked with the entire destinationCalendar array, but the Office 365, Lark, and CalDAV adapters select only the first entry. For example, with two Office 365 hosts, the second host's token attempts to create an event in the first host's calendar rather than its own. This normally fails; CalDAV can instead filter out all calendars and return success without creating anything. Scope the event to the current destination or make all adapters select by credentialId, as the Google adapter does.

findings.title: Retain collective destinations when the organizer has no calendar
findings.body: The event initializes destinationCalendar to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination. The optional push then discards all collected teamDestinationCalendars, even when other collective hosts have connected calendars. Initialize an array and append the other hosts' destinations so those hosts still receive calendar events.

findings.title: Reconstruct collective host destinations when confirming a booking
findings.body: Confirmation reconstructs destinationCalendar using only the booking's single persisted destination or the confirming user's destination. The new-booking handler collects other collective hosts' destinations only in memory, and no calendar events are created until confirmation for pending bookings. Consequently, confirming a collective booking still creates an event for just one host. The confirmation path needs to recover the participating hosts' destinations as well; the payment webhook creation paths have the same omission.

findings.title: Restore a usable Google calendar fallback for references without an external ID
findings.body: When externalCalendarId is null or absent, this fallback searches for a destination whose externalId equals that missing value. Valid destinations have string IDs, so the search always returns undefined and events.update is called without its required calendarId. Older references without externalCalendarId can no longer be rescheduled even when the event has a valid destination. The analogous delete fallback now silently targets primary instead of the configured destination, potentially leaving the event undeleted.

findings.title: Preserve credential IDs on video booking references
findings.body: Reference creation now sets credentialId to undefined for every non-calendar result, whereas previously it preserved result.credentialId for video meetings. The cancellation handler deletes a video meeting only when its booking reference has a credentialId. Newly created dedicated video meetings therefore lose the information needed for cancellation and remain active at the provider after the booking is cancelled.

findings.title: Cancel recurring events using each host's matching reference and credential
findings.body: In the allRemainingBookings branch, the resolved credential for the current calendar reference is ignored. Instead, each outer reference repeats a traversal of only the organizer's credentials, and each recurring booking contributes only its first calendar reference. Other collective hosts' credentials fetched from the database are never used, so their recurring calendar events remain scheduled even though all bookings are marked cancelled. Iterate each updated booking's calendar references and resolve the matching credential for each one.

findings.title: Do not reverse organization slug assignment based on billing
findings.body: This changes slug assignment from !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED while requestedSlug remains conditional on billing being enabled. With team billing disabled, newly created organizations now receive neither slug nor requestedSlug, despite the handler configuring a domain using the requested slug. With billing enabled, the slug is assigned immediately rather than kept as a requested slug. Restore the original condition unless the organization publication flow is intentionally being changed and updated alongside it.
